original_question: Which disease, characterized by itchy red papules centered on hair follicles and typically located on the upper body, is caused by a lentivirus and is commonly associated with advanced HIV infection?

final_qi.question: Which disease, characterized by itchy red papules centered on hair follicles and typically located on the upper body, is caused by a lentivirus and is commonly associated with advanced HIV infection?
final_qi.search_keyword: disease itchy red papules hair follicles lentivirus advanced HIV
final_qi.long_answer: Eosinophilic folliculitis is a skin condition that presents with intensely itchy red papules centered on hair follicles, primarily affecting the upper body. This condition is most commonly seen in patients with advanced HIV infection, which is caused by a lentivirus. The immunocompromised state in advanced HIV leads to an exaggerated inflammatory response, resulting in the characteristic lesions of eosinophilic folliculitis. Its diagnosis is important in the context of HIV management, as its presence may indicate progression of the underlying immunosuppressive disease.
